description: Clean (non-instrumented) wall-clock speedup of incremental KV-cache vs full-recompute speculative decoding, at a longer generation length (400 new tokens) than the initial 60-token test.
caveats: outputs_match=false in all 3 runs is expected, not a bug: temperature=1.0 sampling mode, already diagnosed via scripts/p5_kv_cache_diagnose.py as benign floating-point-noise cascade between the two compute paths. Greedy mode is the strict correctness signal and was separately verified as exact-match (see p5_kv_cache_verify_result).

This speedup (1.651x) is higher than the 1.249x measured by the instrumented scripts/p5_kv_cache_profile.py at the same 400-token length, because profiling instrumentation (extra torch.mps.synchronize() calls) adds overhead that disproportionately penalizes the cached path, which makes many more, smaller model calls per round. This 1.651x, from the non-instrumented script, is the number to cite as the real-world figure.

no_cache run-to-run variance (std=16.9s, ~22% of mean) is much larger than cached (std=4.2s, ~9% of mean) -- noted as an observation (possibly thermal/scheduling variance under sustained load on a single Mac), not investigated further; does not affect the correctness or the direction of the speedup conclusion.

At a short length (60 tokens), the same comparison showed the OPPOSITE result (cached ~0.74x-0.80x, i.e. slower) -- see p5_kv_cache_speedup_result.json and p5_kv_cache_profile_result. The crossover with sequence length is itself the finding; see reports/v1.2_kv_cache.md.
